title: Eng leads weekly: signal and actions - 2027-03-22
content:
Meeting: Cross-team engineering leadership weekly catch-up
Date: 2027-03-22 10:00-11:00 PT
Organizer: Aisha Patel (platform eng)
Attendees: Aisha Patel (platform), Ethan Kim (serving-runtime), Samantha Liu (observability), Diego Morales (private-deployments), Hannah Cho (release-eng), plus ad-hoc reps from infra and solutions (minute notes)

Purpose and framing
- Short, signal-focused sync: surface any cross-team production regressions, major blockers to roadmaps, and 1–2 coordination asks per team.
- Goal for this run: prioritize actions that remove ops/launch friction for next Dedicated capacity wave.

Quick signals (2-minute flashes)
- Serving-runtime: latency p95 has a small uptick in eu-west-1 for 2-token bursts (seen since 03/19). Preliminary kernel pin suspected. Investigation open: INF-4123.
- Observability: new SLO heatmap shows increase in request-level errors tied to a new model variant rollout; need model telemetry tag on routed requests (missing today).
- Private Deployments: one on-prem pilot completed smoke tests, found KMS integration edge-case for HSM rotation; mitigation documented but requires release-engineering support for packaging.
- Release Engineering: weekly release cadence held; one hotfix for autoscaling policy shipped 03/21. Need to validate rollback path for canary failures.
- Platform Engineering: autoscaler policy change candidate that reduces cold-starts by 18% in our lab traces; low-risk rollout plan ready pending infra signoff.

Metrics snapshot (top-level)
- Host API 7d avg p50/p95 latency: 22ms / 210ms (p95 up 14ms WoW)
- Error rate (500s) global: 0.35% (up from 0.18% two weeks ago)
- Dedicated capacity utilization: 63% steady; two customers near committed burst limits
- Infra costs: GPU spot reclaim events causing small tail-latency spikes (FYI)

Incidents & active investigations
1) INF-4123: eu-west-1 p95 regression (serving-runtime)
   - Summary: p95 for short requests increased after kernel/driver update rolled 03/18. Repro in canary region.
   - Owner: Ethan Kim
   - Current state: profiling shows increased kernel runtime on quantized paths for small sequence lengths. Reverted kernel to previous build reduces p95 to baseline.
   - Immediate ask: infra team to hold further driver rollout until hotpatch tested in canary (action item below).

2) OBS-2041: missing model variant telemetry (observability)
   - Summary: model routing decisions aren't tagged in traces for ~3% of requests post new routing policy. Hard to link errors to variants.
   - Owner: Samantha Liu
   - Current state: tracing change rolled, but downstream processors drop tag when message size threshold exceeded. Short-term: increase tag sampling for routed requests. Medium-term: RPC schema change planned.

Cross-team coordination items (discussion notes)
- Autoscaler rollout sequencing: Platform has a low-risk plan to publish new policy; Release Eng requested a one-week freeze on infra driver changes to avoid interacting with autoscaler behavior. Decision: freeze infra driver rollout for 5 working days starting 03/23; platform to run extended soak tests.
- Private deployment packaging: Private-Deployments needs release-eng help to include HSM rotation test in the on-prem bundle. Diego to open PLAT-98 with packaging checklists.
- Canary and fallback policies: Serving-runtime proposes to add an explicit fallback model route for latency-sensitive endpoints (cost trade-offs discussed). Team to prototype in staging and report by 03/29.

Decisions made
- Infra driver rollouts will be paused for 5 business days starting 03/23 (agreed by infra, platform, release).
- Increase tracing sampling for routed requests for two weeks to collect variant-level error signals.
- Prioritize INF-4123 as P0 for the week until kernel behavior is understood and mitigated.

Action items (owner — due)
- Ethan Kim — Pause kernel/driver rollout in eu-west-1 and coordinate with infra to revert candidate on canary clusters (due 2027-03-23).
- Samantha Liu — Implement higher sampling for routed requests and create short dashboard to show variant-level error rates (due 2027-03-24).
- Diego Morales — Open PLAT-98 packaging ticket with HSM rotation test acceptance criteria and link to pilot cluster logs (due 2027-03-24).
- Hannah Cho — Add rollback playbook entry for canary failures triggered by autoscaler interactions; run tabletop with leads (due 2027-03-26).
- Platform Eng (labeled owner: Aisha Patel) — Execute 72h soak of autoscaler policy in staging and publish outcomes (due 2027-03-29).

Risks and escalations
- If kernel patch causes regressions across regions, we risk SLA impact; contingency is to auto-fallback affected regions to last-known-good kernel build. Need infra automation to speed that fallback.
- Observability gaps (missing telemetry) reduce our ability to triage model regressions; extended sampling could incur minor ingestion cost — approved for 2 weeks only.

Notes / open questions
- Should we gate model variant rollouts by observability coverage? (Action: product-hosted-api to propose minimal telemetry contract for rollouts by 03/26.)
- How aggressive should we be with autoscaler rollout given live customer Dedicated pools? (Discuss with CS on Monday.)

Follow-ups and owners for next meeting
- Quick readout on INF-4123 status (Ethan)
- Autoscaler soak results (Aisha / Platform)
- Packaging ticket and pilot follow-up (Diego)
- Variant-level error dashboard (Samantha)

Appendix: links and quick refs
- INF-4123 (jira): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123
- Autoscaler rollout plan (confluence): confluence://space/PLAT/autoscaler-rollout-2027
- Serving-runtime PR that introduced kernel candidate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2847

End of notes.
